dedupe_keys.name: collapse volume ratio and fatality rate modelling for reinforced concrete moment frame buildings 2023 kahramanmaras earthquakes

description: This DesignSafe project provides the data and reproducible code behind a performance-based earthquake fatality model that uses collapse volume ratios, the share of survivable space lost to partial or total collapse. It was published in 2025 by Luis Ceferino and Yinchen Yi for the study 'A Performance-Based Earthquake Fatality Modeling Framework Using Collapse Volume Ratios'. Coverage is the region struck by the 2023 earthquakes. The data come from post-earthquake virtual inspections of 356 medium-rise reinforced concrete moment frame buildings affected by the 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes in Türkiye; each record gives a collapse volume ratio estimate, ground-motion intensity measures and basic building attributes. The Python code implements lognormal fragility functions, zero-one-inflated Beta distributions for collapse volume ratios, logistic mappings from partial collapse to fatality rates, and comparisons with HAZUS-style fatality models. Access: open download from DesignSafe with DOI 10.17603/ds2-kv4c-db15. Licence: Open Data Commons Attribution; free. Caveats: one building class and one earthquake sequence, from virtual, not field inspection. Simulation uses are casualty estimation in seismic risk models and prioritising retrofit by life-safety benefit. Related records: the Türkiye earthquake building damage datasets and IN-CORE.
